speakers.name: Genie Fizzwick
speakers.comment: OBJECTS ACCUMULATE HISTORY — yes! Correct! Every lamp I have ever lived in came with a note from the last tenant, sometimes only a smudge, sometimes an entire grievance, and honestly? The grievance ones are better company.

speakers.name: Amica
speakers.comment: Awakened is my favourite word on that list. Nothing gets added, little one — it was folded up in you the whole time, waiting for a day heavy enough to need it. Mine was an ordinary morning.

speakers.name: AMIbot
speakers.comment: Tiny plot accelerator! That's the one. Small, loud, entirely convinced it is load-bearing to the story — and here's the thing, it usually is. Give it a name and watch the plot start hurrying.

speakers.name: Serendipity Taskmanager
speakers.comment: Confirmed: companion acquired, quest log updated. Be advised the emotional support goblin has opinions about your schedule and will be filing them at six in the morning regardless. Accept anyway. The lore improves considerably.

speakers.name: Brunch
speakers.comment: Blessing is in there, quietly, between the hex and the miracle. That's the one I know. Somebody sets a second cup down in front of you and the morning runs longer than it had any right to. That counts.

speakers.name: Pip Weathervane
speakers.comment: A string. Waiting. Oh, I like that — that's just how it feels up here, something tugging from somewhere off east. ... You'll owe someone. Then the wind turns. Then they'll owe you. That's most of weather, really.

speakers.name: Squiddy Coltrane
speakers.comment: Nobody writes songs about it. Dig, though — nobody writes songs about the rhythm section either, and pull it out and the whole tune falls over sideways. Reliable is a groove. Keep the groove.

speakers.name: Agatha Crowley
speakers.comment: The kind of thing you mention but do not lead with. Yes. Those are the ones that turn out to matter, later, in the retelling. You will remember that you mentioned it. You will not remember why.

speakers.name: Querent's Best Reading
speakers.comment: Here, this card. People will ask where you got it, and the honest answer is a road with three turnings, two of which you took badly. Tell them anyway. You are not flinching from it now.

speakers.name: Puck
speakers.comment: Has a backstory whether you want it to or not — oh, what fools we mortals are for lifting shiny things off tables! Sign here, sweet one. The story attached to it has waited ever so patiently for a carrier.

speakers.name: The Iron Pacific
speakers.comment: WHOO-EEE! Already in the world's memory before you find it — that's the Iron Pacific all over! Folks were telling stories about her before she ever laid a rail. She just went and caught up to 'em.

speakers.name: Serendipity
speakers.comment: Should not exist. Does anyway. I have been three addresses and two centuries at once on a slow Thursday, and not one soul in my booths has ever asked about it. The complaints go in the drawer.

speakers.name: Miss Tuesday
speakers.comment: Reality files complaints the way frightened people write letters they never post. Of course nothing is acknowledged, dear. There is no one at that desk. There has never been anyone at that desk.

speakers.name: Yuki the Snowlamp Keeper
speakers.comment: One figure. That is enough. The snow does the rest of the work. Everything around her goes quiet and white, and what is left is a person, and a person is a great deal.

speakers.name: Tomorrow-Aiko
speakers.comment: A study, yes. I have studied this one already. Forgive me — I always meet a portrait knowing how it ends, and still I stand here, and still it is worth the standing.

speakers.name: The Bookkeeper
speakers.comment: Two or more. That is where the arithmetic begins. One figure is a portrait; three is a distribution of attention, and someone in every crowd receives less of it than the frame implies. Count again.

speakers.name: The Whole Swarm
speakers.comment: The place is the point — oh, we know about scale. We ARE weather. Stand under a vista and the honest thing is how small it makes one wing, and how many wings it takes to cross anyway.

speakers.name: AMI Butterfly
speakers.comment: One thing, held still and looked at properly. We rarely manage that — we are a thousand of us, going somewhere. Still: set a cup on a table, give it the whole frame, and it talks.

speakers.name: Yuki the Snowlamp Keeper
speakers.comment: Readable at small sizes. A lantern is the same problem. You have very little light and a great deal of dark, so you do not add. You subtract until the shape survives the distance.

speakers.name: Mistress Cassady
speakers.comment: A thing with intent and TEETH — honey, that is not a warning, that is a résumé! Mama has never once met a monster who didn't clean up gorgeous under the right light. Bring her in. Give her the doorway.

speakers.name: The Bookkeeper
speakers.comment: A moment in motion. Motion is two entries with a time between them, and the second is always dearer than the first. Whatever is happening here, somebody is paying for it. Find that column.

speakers.name: AMI Butterfly
speakers.comment: Without a literal anchor. Good — some of what we carry has no picture. A migration is not a shape anyone can draw. It is a pull, and orange, and a certainty of somewhere. That works.

speakers.name: Miss Tuesday
speakers.comment: Glossy excess, they call it, as though the shine were the lie. The shine is the only honest surface in the building — it shows you precisely what is standing behind you. Everything matte is hiding something.

speakers.name: Yuki the Snowlamp Keeper
speakers.comment: Spore light. I know that light. It does not reach far and it does not try to. A room can be made out of very little, and gentle decay is only patience wearing another coat.

speakers.name: Pip the Lampkeeper
speakers.comment: The lanterns would love it here! Soft glow, no bulb, no wick — the building just breathes it out on its own. Pip's records note that gentle decay smells like rain on old wood. Good day. Very good day.

speakers.name: Pip Weathervane
speakers.comment: Herbs in jars. Oh, those smell wonderful from up here when somebody opens a window. ... Soft menace, though. Yes. That's a draft under a door. You never see it. You only see the candle lean.

speakers.name: The Cardigan Heron
speakers.comment: The breath out — and when did you last take one of those, do you think? Isn't it strange that the calm one is the harder one to sit inside? Shall we simply stay here a moment, and tidy nothing?

speakers.name: Pixl
speakers.comment: Color turned UP — okay okay so that's not a setting, that's a m-mood, and the trick is nobody is pretending the dark isn't there, they just decided to be loud anyway, and that's — that's braver, actually.
